en: to be absorbed in; to be immersed in; to fall into

examples.en: I got so absorbed in the novel that I missed my stop.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 방에 누우니 금방 깊은 잠에 빠져들었어요.
examples.en: Lying down in the warm room, I quickly fell into a deep sleep.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 보면 볼수록 빠져들게 돼요.
examples.en: The more you watch this drama, the more you get hooked.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 목소리에 빠져드는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people get drawn into that singer's voice.

examples.ko: 그는 깊은 생각에 빠져든 채 말이 없었어요.
examples.en: He was lost in deep thought and said nothing.

examples.ko: 한번 게임에 빠져들면 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.
examples.en: Once I get absorbed in a game, I lose track of time.

explain: '빠지다'가 갑자기 빠지는 느낌이라면 '빠져들다'는 점점 깊이 들어가는 느낌이에요. '잠, 생각, 이야기, 노래'처럼 마음을 빼앗기는 것에 '~에 빠져들다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I was so tired that I fell into a deep sleep as soon as I lay down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠이 점점 깊어지는 느낌을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the feeling of sleep getting gradually deeper.

phrases.example: 영화 속 이야기에 빠져들어서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
phrases.en: I was so drawn into the movie's story that I lost track of time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책, 영화, 음악 같은 것에 마음이 점점 끌려 들어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your mind is slowly drawn into a book, film, or music.
phrases.en_equiv: to get absorbed in a story

phrases.example: 창밖을 보다가 혼자 깊은 생각에 빠져들었어요.
phrases.en: Looking out the window, I sank into deep thought on my own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변을 잊을 만큼 생각이 깊어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when thoughts get so deep you forget your surroundings.

explain_en: Everyday; sinking into a story, game or feeling (소설에 빠져들다) '빠지다' can feel like a sudden fall, while '빠져들다' feels like gradually going deeper. It is used as '~에 빠져들다' for things that capture your mind, such as sleep, thoughts, stories and songs.

en: to admit; to acknowledge; to concede

examples.en: He admitted his mistake right away.
The company admitted its mistake and apologized.
We were surprised because my friend admitted the lie.
It is not easy to admit your mistakes.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 규칙을 어긴 것을 시인할 거예요.
examples.en: The player will admit that he broke the rules.
He never admitted it, so the problem dragged on.

explain: 숨기고 싶은 잘못이나 사실을 인정할 때 써요. 뉴스와 공식적인 자리에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '인정하다'가 더 흔해요. 같은 소리의 '시인'은 시를 쓰는 사람(poet)이라서 문장 속 위치로 구분해요.

phrases.en: I admit my mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시인하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '시인하다' and far more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: He admitted his fault and apologized.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시인하다'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word partner for '시인하다'.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 끝까지 사실을 시인하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He never admitted the truth to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실이나 잘못을 끝까지 말하지 않을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when someone refuses to own up.

explain_en: Formal — admit a fault or wrongdoing. Used when someone admits a fault or a fact they wanted to hide. It shows up in news and formal settings; in daily talk '인정하다' is more common. The word '시인' with the same sound also means a poet, so read it by context.

dis.h: formal; admit a fault or wrongdoing
gh: everyday; accept as true, or recognize ability

p.n: The other word is more everyday and also works for recognizing ability.

t90.ax: He admitted his mistake right away.

examples.ko: 한국에 와서 겨울이 춥다는 걸 실감했어요.
examples.en: I really felt how cold winter is after coming to Korea.
It still hasn't sunk in that I've graduated.
Even after hearing the news of my acceptance, it was hard to take in.

examples.ko: 물가가 오른 것을 장을 볼 때 실감해요.
examples.en: I feel prices going up when I go grocery shopping.

examples.ko: 직접 가 보면 이 도시의 크기를 실감할 거예요.
examples.en: If you go there yourself, you will feel how big this city is.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우며 부모님의 마음을 실감하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people truly feel their parents' hearts while raising a child.

explain: '실감하다'는 머리로 알던 일을 직접 겪고서 확 와닿을 때 써요. 부정은 '실감하지 못하다'와 '실감이 안 나다' 둘 다 자주 말해요. 믿기지 않는 좋은 일이 생겼을 때 '실감이 안 나요'라는 말이 특히 흔해요.

phrases.en: I'm only now feeling that I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 진짜로 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something finally feels real.

phrases.example: 결혼했다는 게 아직 실감이 안 나요.
phrases.en: It still doesn't feel real that I got married.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿기지 않는 큰 일이 생겼을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said about big events that are hard to believe.

phrases.example: 혼자 살면서 부모님의 사랑을 실감하게 됐어요.
phrases.en: Living alone, I came to really feel my parents' love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험을 통해 점점 알게 된다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests coming to understand through experience.

explain_en: '실감하다' is used when something you knew in your head hits home after you experience it. The negative is said both as '실감하지 못하다' and '실감이 안 나다'. When something unbelievably good happens, '실감이 안 나요' is especially common.

examples.en: My self-control weakens in front of sweet food.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 자제력을 잃으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you are angry, you must not lose your self-control.

examples.ko: 야식을 참다니 정말 자제력 있는 분이네요.
examples.en: You resisted a late-night snack, so you really have self-control.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 자제력을 기르는 연습이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need to practice building self-control from childhood.
Self-control doesn't develop overnight.
At the last moment I held back my words through self-control.

explain: 하고 싶은 것이나 화를 스스로 멈추는 힘을 말해요. '참을성'은 힘든 것을 견디는 쪽이고, 자제력은 해 버리고 싶은 것을 스스로 멈추는 쪽에 가까워요. '자제력을 잃다/기르다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 동생은 자제력이 부족해서 게임을 오래 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling lacks self-control and plays games for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 멈추지 못하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone can't stop themselves.

phrases.en: Even though I was angry, I held back my words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자제력'의 동사 모양으로, 하고 싶은 걸 스스로 참을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb related to the headword, used for holding oneself back.

phrases.en: Raising a child takes patience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자제력은 하고 싶은 걸 멈추는 힘이고, 참을성은 힘든 걸 견디는 힘이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Self-control stops what you want to do; this is the ability to endure hardship.

explain_en: Ability to restrain one's own desires or emotions (자제력이 부족하다). It is the power to stop yourself from doing what you want or from getting angry. '참을성' leans toward enduring hardship, while '자제력' leans toward stopping yourself from acting on an urge. Common patterns are '자제력을 잃다/기르다'.

examples.ko: 그는 회의 중에 갑자기 폭탄선언을 했어요.
examples.en: He suddenly dropped a bombshell during the meeting.
Everyone was shocked by the boss's sudden bombshell announcement.

examples.ko: 유명 배우의 결혼 폭탄선언이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A famous actor's surprise marriage announcement was in the news.

examples.ko: 폭탄선언은 가족과 미리 상의한 뒤에 하세요.
examples.en: Talk it over with your family before making a bombshell announcement.

examples.ko: 친구의 폭탄선언 뒤에 한참 동안 조용했어요.
examples.en: It was quiet for a long time after my friend's bombshell.

examples.ko: 딸이 퇴사하겠다고 폭탄선언해서 집이 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: My daughter shocked us by announcing she'd quit her job, and the house was in an uproar.

explain: 모두가 예상하지 못한 중요한 발표에 써요. 뉴스에서는 '폭탄 발언'이라고도 해요. 보통 '폭탄선언을 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 폭탄 발언이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: The singer's bombshell remark was on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 한 놀라운 말을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a single shocking remark.

phrases.en: A surprising bombshell announcement came at the end of the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 중요한 발표가 나왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an unexpected big announcement is made.

phrases.en: My friend made a surprise bombshell announcement at the gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깜짝'을 붙이면 더 놀라운 느낌이 나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 깜짝 makes the surprise stronger.

explain_en: It is used for an important announcement nobody expected. News also uses '폭탄 발언' in a similar way. The usual pattern is '폭탄선언을 하다'.

examples.en: I shifted the car's gear to third.

examples.ko: 자전거 기어가 고장 나서 수리점에 갔어요.
examples.en: The bicycle gear broke, so I went to the repair shop.
Shift to a lower gear when climbing a hill.

examples.ko: 시계 안에는 작은 기어가 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: A watch has many small gears inside.

examples.ko: 운전 연습을 하다가 기어를 잘못 넣었어요.
examples.en: While practicing driving, I put it in the wrong gear.
The gears mesh together and the machine turns.

explain: 기어는 자동차나 자전거에서 속도와 힘을 바꾸는 장치나 바퀴를 말해요. 자동차에서는 '기어를 넣다', '기어를 바꾸다'처럼 말해요. '기어가다'의 '기어'(기다+어)와 글자가 같아서 문장을 보고 구별해요.

phrases.en: I put the car in gear to start moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차를 움직이게 하려고 기어를 맞출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for putting a car in gear to make it move.

phrases.en: You have to change gears on a hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차나 자전거의 속도와 힘을 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for changing speed and power on a car or bike.

phrases.en: The gear won't go in well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기어가 잘 맞지 않는 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a problem where the gear won't shift properly.

explain_en: 기어 is a gear in a car or bicycle, the part that changes speed and force. For cars you say '기어를 넣다' or '기어를 바꾸다'. The verb form '기어' (from 기다, to crawl, as in 기어가다) is written the same, so check the sentence to tell them apart.

examples.en: It's the tail end of winter, so mornings are still cold.
I met my friend at the far end of the alley.
The closing part of that movie is moving.
I walked holding the hem of my skirt.
It rained at the very end of my vacation.
There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.

explain: 그냥 '끝'보다 천천히 끝나 가는 부분이라는 느낌이 있어요. 계절과 휴가 같은 때에는 '가을의 끝자락'처럼, 옷과 골목 같은 곳에는 '치마 끝자락'처럼 써요. '마지막'은 딱 하나뿐인 맨 뒤를 말해요.

phrases.en: It's the tail end of winter, so the wind is still a bit cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이 천천히 끝나 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a season is slowly coming to an end.

phrases.en: There is a small cafe at the far end of the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이나 장소의 맨 끝 쪽을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the far edge of a road or place.

phrases.en: The hem of my skirt got wet from the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷의 아래쪽 끝부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the bottom edge of clothing.

explain_en: Very last fringe of a season or place; literary feel. It feels like a part that is slowly ending, rather than a plain 끝 (end). It works for times, as in '가을의 끝자락' (the tail end of autumn), and for places or things like '치마 끝자락' (hem of a skirt). 마지막 means the very last one.

dis.h: Very last edge or tail of a period or place
gh: General end of anything, place or time

p.n: 끝 is a plain end point; 끝자락 means the fading tail part.

examples.en: The company stores customer information in a database.
The database broke down, so the site stopped.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 단어를 데이터베이스에서 찾아 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This app finds words in a database and shows them.
I am learning how to build a database.

examples.ko: 새 데이터베이스로 옮기는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Moving to the new database took a day.
I searched for papers in the library database.

explain: 'DB'라고 줄여 쓰고, 말로는 '디비'라고 읽어요. 보통 '데이터베이스에 저장하다', '데이터베이스에서 찾다'처럼 에/에서와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I saved the customer information in the DB.
phrases.nuance_ko: '데이터베이스'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때는 '디비'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortening of 데이터베이스, pronounced '디비' in speech.

phrases.en: I found the name in the database.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보를 검색할 때 '에서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 에서 when searching for information.
phrases.en_equiv: to look up in a database

phrases.en: He manages the company database.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 사람이 데이터베이스를 맡을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who takes care of a database at work.

explain_en: It is shortened to 'DB' in writing and read aloud as '디비'. It usually appears with the particles 에/에서, as in '데이터베이스에 저장하다' (save to the database) and '데이터베이스에서 찾다' (search in the database).

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 사나흘 동안 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to school for three or four days because of a cold.
I'm planning to go on a trip for three or four days.

examples.ko: 이 김치는 사나흘 뒤에 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: This kimchi tastes good after three or four days.
It has been raining for three or four days straight.
The item you ordered will arrive in three or four days.

examples.ko: 일이 많아서 사나흘은 밤을 새워야 해요.
examples.en: I have so much work that I'll need to stay up nights for three or four days.

explain: 사흘이나 나흘쯤 되는 기간을 대충 말할 때 써요. 정확한 숫자보다 '대략 그 정도'라는 느낌이라서 일정이나 기간을 말할 때 편해요. 같은 느낌으로 '이삼일', '삼사일'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The rain stopped after three or four days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-만에'가 붙어서 그 기간이 지난 뒤에 일어난 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -만에, it describes something that happened after that stretch of time.

phrases.en: I'll contact you again in three or four days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 다른 말이에요. 숫자를 한자어로 말해서 조금 더 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another word for the same span. It uses Sino-Korean numbers, so it sounds a bit more formal.

phrases.en: It takes about three or four days for the package to arrive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걸리는 시간을 대략 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to give a rough estimate of how long something takes.
phrases.en_equiv: takes about three or four days

explain_en: It refers to a period of roughly three or four days, so it feels approximate rather than exact, which is handy for schedules. '이삼일' and '삼사일' give a similar feel.

examples.ko: 오늘은 여느 날과 다르게 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: Today I woke up early, unlike any usual day.
I had coffee and went to work as usual.

examples.ko: 그 집 음식은 여느 식당보다 맛있어요.
examples.en: That place's food tastes better than at an ordinary restaurant.
Like any other kid, he likes comics.
This winter is colder than an average year.
That day started just like any other weekend.

explain: '여느'는 항상 뒤에 명사가 와요. '여느 때/날/사람'처럼 쓰고 보통 '~와 다르다', '~처럼', '~보다'가 따라와요. '다른'은 서로 같지 않다는 뜻이고 '여느'는 '평범한'이라는 뜻이라 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요.

phrases.en: Today I was busier than usual.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보다'와 함께 평소와 비교할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 보다 to compare with the usual.

phrases.en: It's an ordinary morning like any other day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-과 같다'와 함께 평범한 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -과 같다 to describe an ordinary day.

phrases.example: 저도 여느 사람처럼 평범하게 살고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to live an ordinary life like anyone else.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-처럼'과 함께 보통 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -처럼 to mean an ordinary person.

explain_en: '여느' must always be followed by a noun, as in '여느 때', '여느 날' and '여느 사람', and is usually followed by '~와 다르다', '~처럼' or '~보다'. '다른' means not the same, but '여느' means ordinary, so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.en: It's market day, so there's a lot to see at the market.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 오 일에 한 번 장날이 서요.
examples.en: In our town, market day comes once every five days.
Grandma goes out to sell vegetables every market day.

examples.ko: 장날에 가면 싱싱한 나물을 싸게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go on market day, you can buy fresh greens cheaply.
Do you know when the next market day is?
Today is market day, so the roads are really jammed.

explain: 오일장처럼 정해진 날에 열리는 시장이 서는 날이에요. 요즘 도시에서는 매일 가게가 열려서 시골이나 전통 시장 이야기에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 그 식당에 갔는데 가는 날이 장날이라고 문을 닫았더라고요.
phrases.en: I went to that restaurant for the first time in a while, and just my luck, it was closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 있어서 갔더니 공교롭게도 일이 꼬였을 때 쓰는 속담이에요. 보통 운이 나쁘거나 타이밍이 안 맞았을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb for when you go somewhere and things unluckily turn out wrong. It is mostly said about bad luck or bad timing.

explain_en: It is the day a periodic market, like a five-day market, is held. Because city shops open every day, it appears mostly in talk about the countryside and traditional markets.

examples.en: I made a flower shape with wire.
The wire is bent, so it's hard to straighten.
We put up a wire fence in the garden.
I put on gloves and held the wire carefully.
My clothes tore after catching on a wire.
This wire is thin, so it breaks easily.

explain: '전선'은 전기가 흐르는 줄이고, '철사'는 모양을 잡거나 묶을 때 쓰는 금속 줄이에요. 꽃가게나 만들기 수업에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I tied the flowers with wire to make a bouquet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈 대신 단단히 고정할 때 철사를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Wire is used instead of string to fasten things firmly.

phrases.en: I bent the wire to make a heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만들기 수업에서 모양을 만들 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in craft classes when shaping something.

phrases.en: The dry cleaner gave me a wire hanger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철사로 만든 옷걸이예요. 세탁소에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: A hanger made of wire, often seen at dry cleaners.

explain_en: 전선 is a cable that carries electricity, while 철사 is a metal wire used to shape or tie things. It is often used in flower shops and craft classes.

examples.en: The ship leaves port at seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 어제는 배가 출항하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, the ship could not leave port yesterday.
The fishermen set out to sea at dawn.
I waved at the ship that was leaving port.
If the weather clears up, we will set sail tomorrow.
The cruise ship leaves port in Busan and goes to Japan.

explain: '출항하다'는 배에만 써요. 비행기가 떠날 때는 '이륙하다', 버스나 기차는 '출발하다'를 써요. 반대로 배가 항구에 들어오는 것은 '입항하다'예요.

phrases.en: What time is the departure?
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 떠나는 시간을 물을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to ask when a ship leaves.

phrases.en: The ship delayed its departure because of bad weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출항하다'를 명사처럼 써서 '미루다'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun form with 'to postpone'.

phrases.en: The ship cannot leave port because the wind is strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 떠나고 싶어도 떠날 수 없는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a ship that cannot leave even though it wants to.

explain_en: Mainly a ship leaving port; can also mean an aircraft departing (항구에서 출항하다) '출항하다' is used only for ships. A plane taking off is '이륙하다', and buses and trains use '출발하다'. The opposite, a ship entering a harbor, is '입항하다'.

dis.h: a ship leaves port to sail
gh: leave one's country, e.g. by plane
leave a place; general, neutral verb

p.n: 출발하다 is general; 출항하다 is only for ships leaving port.

t90.ax: The fishermen set out to sea at dawn.
